claims.claim: Applied Digital's defensible structural role is not generic AI demand but access to grid-connected, power-dense campus capacity that can be converted into long-duration hyperscaler leases; this is a real bottleneck while interconnection and powered-shell supply remain constrained.

The bottleneck is not permanent: utilities, competing developers and hyperscalers' own-build programs can add substitute capacity, so durable value depends on delivering energized campuses on time and preserving acceptable project returns rather than merely announcing contracted megawatts.
Long take-or-pay leases reduce demand uncertainty but shift the dominant causal risk toward construction, utility/interconnect, financing and tenant-concentration execution.

causalEdges.mechanism: large accelerator clusters require scarce power, interconnection and purpose-built cooling/electrical infrastructure
causalEdges.falsifier: regional powered capacity expands faster than demand or compute efficiency materially reduces required site power

causalEdges.mechanism: completed and energized campuses begin lease economics under long-duration commitments
causalEdges.falsifier: construction/interconnection delays, tenant default/cancellation, or project economics fail to convert contracted capacity into durable cash returns

causalEdges.from: scarce interconnection and campus delivery capability
causalEdges.mechanism: lead times and utility constraints make near-term substitute capacity slow to replicate
causalEdges.falsifier: competitors or hyperscalers add comparable energized capacity with shorter lead times or superior economics

risks.risk: Successor bottleneck shifts from demand capture to capital availability, utility delivery and construction execution as contracted capacity scales.
Site-specific scarcity can erode as competing campuses and utility upgrades expand regional supply.

unknowns.unknown: Project-level unlevered returns and tenant-by-tenant concentration are not fully disclosed in inherited evidence.
Exact regional substitute-capacity pipeline is not canonical in this packet.

claims.claim: The strongest present-day challenge is capital structure/execution, not absence of demand: inherited FY2026 evidence shows about $5.0B debt versus about $4.2B cash plus restricted cash while GAAP losses remained material.
Share count growth of roughly 36.8% year over year is a concrete dilution warning and prevents treating enterprise growth as equivalent to per-share value creation.

More than 1 GW contracted capacity and $31B baseline contracted revenue are meaningful demand signals but are not equivalent to delivered capacity, recognized revenue, free cash flow or project return; backlog/TAM inflation must therefore be resisted.

No current evidence in the inherited packet falsifies the core demand thesis; risks are material but presently non-gating because identity, primary provenance and reproducible methodology treatment are intact.

causalEdges.mechanism: large pre-revenue construction commitments require debt/equity capital before stabilized lease cash flows
causalEdges.falsifier: internally generated cash and non-dilutive project financing consistently fund expansion without worsening leverage or per-share economics

risks.risk: Leverage and continued GAAP losses can overwhelm contracted-demand strength if delivery slips or refinancing costs rise.
Tenant concentration can create asymmetric renegotiation/default exposure even under long contracts.
High headline contracted revenue may create confidence inflation if investors ignore build cost, timing and project-level returns.
Competing powered campuses and hyperscaler self-build are credible substitutes over the medium term.

unknowns.unknown: Normalized free-cash-flow economics excluding fit-out revenue are not established by inherited evidence.
Tenant identities and concentration percentages are not fully disclosed in this artifact set.
